verdict.rationale: USCIS publishes Form G-28 as the authorization form and names the roles that may use it: an attorney or accredited representative files it to represent a client. Representatives can file forms online on a client's behalf through a representative account, including subsequent G-28s for certain pending forms, and representatives also have documented case-status API access. The evidence does not show any published limits on what a representative may NOT do, or which signatures must stay personal to the applicant. missing for 10: published boundaries on what representatives cannot do, documentation of which signatures remain personal to the applicant, coverage of other delegate roles (e.g., preparers/interpreters), independent corroboration.
